evidence.quote:
DM: We begin on the skyship Vindristjarna, hovering above the rocky foothills of central Cymea.

DM: As the ship begins to drift into the sky, heading south for the elven kingdom of Orenlas, an old dwarf sits in his cabin writing at a small desk in cramped dwarven runes:

DM: “4 Barukhelm 5881,” he writes. “My first adventure in more than a decade succeeded beyond my wildest imagination. That Seeker fellow sure knows how to pick his friends. I was not sure what to think when I first met them. They seemed rather prone to excessive chatter and terminal indecision. I was afraid it would be like being back on my travels with Lyrial and her friends. So much time sitting around debating, so little time doing. Although I guess it was in one of those rambling discourses that she told me about the Edge of Echoes in the first place. Once we got moving, I couldn't help but wonder at the powerful oddities they carried, and their skill at using them. A folding boat, I've seen, sure, but a mirror that reveals the history of things? That was a sight. And all Seeker's friends proved quite adept at battle. I think I would have been drowned by water elementals if they had not leapt to my defense.

DM: Oh, and flight. To fly again! It was nothing like the flying carpet we borrowed back in the day. To be able to think and just go where you wish—truly something else. Somehow the fey step trick I learned from Lyrial feels cheap in comparison now.

DM: Of course, my goal was to make my dear Pebblepeep fly, and I can't believe how successful I was. I surprise even myself sometimes. Aha!

DM: All that hard work outfitting this ship—oh, this ship! I wonder if they'd let me stay, or maybe even let me fly it someday—was well worth it. It'll be hard going back to life in Tollen after this.”

DM: As the dwarf pauses in his writing and the ship turns to begin its 24 h journey to Orenlas, where you will stop to deliver messages from Melindir and hopefully find somebody who remembers the ancient history of Drankor and Apollyon that might know something of how to fight him.
DM: We begin on the skyship Vindristjarna, hovering above the rocky foothills of central Cymea.

p03.label: inert forge

evidence.quote:
DM: You think back to your vision in the mirror last night.

DM: So, remembering the scene where you, before packing up, held the mirror up to this now inert forge, watching to see its history and what had been created here. The mirror fades, and you see a scene, the forge now brightly lit.

DM: These 4 silvery lightning, wiry threads taut and vibrating with energy as a woman approaches—the same woman you saw, the the programmed illusion, the presumably the Occulta mage, who ran this place towards the end of its time.

p03.note: Physical presence is recalled from the previous night; the mirror scenes show ancient crafting. The Elemental Forge note places the site within Edge of Echoes, retained here as attributed vault orientation rather than transcript-backed containment.

evidence.quote:
DM: We begin on the skyship Vindristjarna, hovering above the rocky foothills of central Cymea.

DM: As the ship begins to drift into the sky, heading south for the elven kingdom of Orenlas, an old dwarf sits in his cabin writing at a small desk in cramped dwarven runes:

DM: “4 Barukhelm 5881,” he writes. “My first adventure in more than a decade succeeded beyond my wildest imagination. That Seeker fellow sure knows how to pick his friends. I was not sure what to think when I first met them. They seemed rather prone to excessive chatter and terminal indecision. I was afraid it would be like being back on my travels with Lyrial and her friends. So much time sitting around debating, so little time doing. Although I guess it was in one of those rambling discourses that she told me about the Edge of Echoes in the first place. Once we got moving, I couldn't help but wonder at the powerful oddities they carried, and their skill at using them. A folding boat, I've seen, sure, but a mirror that reveals the history of things? That was a sight. And all Seeker's friends proved quite adept at battle. I think I would have been drowned by water elementals if they had not leapt to my defense.

DM: Oh, and flight. To fly again! It was nothing like the flying carpet we borrowed back in the day. To be able to think and just go where you wish—truly something else. Somehow the fey step trick I learned from Lyrial feels cheap in comparison now.

DM: Of course, my goal was to make my dear Pebblepeep fly, and I can't believe how successful I was. I surprise even myself sometimes. Aha!

DM: All that hard work outfitting this ship—oh, this ship! I wonder if they'd let me stay, or maybe even let me fly it someday—was well worth it. It'll be hard going back to life in Tollen after this.”

DM: As the dwarf pauses in his writing and the ship turns to begin its 24 h journey to Orenlas, where you will stop to deliver messages from Melindir and hopefully find somebody who remembers the ancient history of Drankor and Apollyon that might know something of how to fight him.
